documents.abstract: Text-Attributed Graphs (TAGs) are prevalent in various real-world scenarios, where each node is associated with a text attribute. Representation learning on TAGs relies on a comprehensive understanding of both the textual attributes and the topological connections. Recent works have enhanced graph neural networks (GNNs) with pre-trained language models (PLMs) for textual attribute modeling, achieving promising results compared with shallow text representations such as BoW. With the advent of more powerful LLMs, how to effectively and efficiently inject the generic knowledge in LLMs into representation learning on TAGs still calls for systematic investigation. To this end, we first examine whether mainstream generative LLMs can provide high-quality generic text embeddings that can be directly used by downstream GNNs, and further explore their complementarity with the task-specific knowledge from a tuned PLM (TLM). Based on these observations, we propose a dual-channel knowledge fusion framework, named MoKGNN, to simultaneously leverage the generic semantic knowledge from LLMs and the task adaptation capability of TLM. Specifically, we design a dual-channel feature extraction module to learn generic and task-specific text representations separately. Next, we introduce a Knowledge Alignment Network to align the LLM embeddings with the TLM representations. Finally, MoKGNN adopts a global mixing weight to fuse the two channels, obtaining a unified node embedding for downstream GNN training. Moreover, we further analyze a key limitation of such early feature fusion under message passing: once heterogeneous text features are merged before neighborhood aggregation, source-specific noise and non-aligned semantics may be diffused together and become harder to disentangle and correct. Motivated by this observation, we propose IMoKGNN, a decoupled dual-stream framework that propagates LLM and TLM features in parallel with a shared GNN backbone and performs late fusion in logit space. Extensive experiments on five TAG datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approaches for both node classification and link prediction, and show that IMoKGNN yields more reliable improvements than MoKGNN.

Abstract The Artificial Intelligence (AI) integration into education is transforming traditional teaching and learning practices. Google Classroom, currently with AI-enabled features such as lesson-plan generation, quiz creation, rubric development, differentiated learning resources, and suggested feedback, provides faculty with special power to improve teaching efficiency and classroom management. This study examines the impact of AI-enabled features on faculty teaching effectiveness in Google Classroom. The study mainly focuses on how AI influences lesson planning, preparation time, assessment, feedback, personalization of learning, student engagement, and overall teaching effectiveness. The study can be conducted using a structured questionnaire among faculty members who use Google Classroom. The findings are expected to show that AI can reduce routine workload and support more efficient and personalized teaching. However, factors such as AI literacy, training, accuracy of AI-generated content, privacy concerns, and the need for human supervision may influence its effectiveness. Research on AI in education also emphasizes the importance of teacher professional development and responsible implementation.

The aim of this study was to determine the effect of Artificial Intelligence (AI) based fitness applications on physical activity participation and health behaviour among the undergraduates of Federal Universities, North-West Nigeria. The four objectives, four research questions, and four null hypotheses were the compass of this study. For the study, a descriptive correlational survey research design was used. The population consisted of undergraduate students of a few Federal Universities in the Northwest Nigeria. 384 undergraduate students were chosen as respondents using a multistage sampling technique. The Artificial Intelligence Fitness Applications, Physical Activity and Health Behaviour Questionnaire (AIFAPHBQ) was used to gather data. The internal consistency of the instrument was evaluated by Cronbach's Alpha reliability technique and the overall reliability coefficient obtained was 0.84. It was endorsed by experts in the field of Physical and Health Education, Educational Technology, and Measurement and Evaluation. The mean and the standard deviation were used to solve the problems in the study, while the independent-samples t-test and Pearson Product Moment Correlation were applied to test the null hypotheses at 0.05 level of significance. Based on the results, the use of AI-based fitness apps among undergraduate students was at moderate level (Grand Mean = 2.84, SD = 0.76). Use of the AI fitness app was positively associated with physical activity participation (r = .61, p < .001) and health behaviour (r = .58, p < .001). The results also revealed that male students felt they were using AI based fitness apps slightly more than female students, but this was not statistically significant (t = 1.63, p = .104). The researchers found that there is significant potential for the use of AI fitness apps to boost physical activity participation and promote positive health behaviours among undergraduate students. It suggests that digital health education, implementing institutional wellness programmes, and enhancing access to relevant digital infrastructure should be encouraged to promote responsible and health-oriented use of AI-based fitness technologies at universities.

Abstract Digital business transformation reshapes traditional operations by integrating modern tools like artificial intelligence and cloud computing to boost efficiency and create new customer value. Digital India improves public service delivery, boosts financial inclusion, and transforms the country into a digitally empowered economy. Systems like Unified Payments Interface and digital bank accounts connect millions of unbanked citizens to the formal financial network. Online portals make government paperwork fast, transparent, and paperless through platforms like Digital India and Digi Locker. Direct Benefit Transfers send subsidies straight to bank accounts, cutting out middlemen and stopping leaks. Digitalization is one of the most powerful development opportunities of our time. Connectivity, data, and digital tools are now essential to how hospitals deliver care, how farmers access markets, how teachers reach students, and how governments serve their citizens.

documents.abstract: Abstract Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) has significantly influenced students' approach to formal writing. The present research, titled “Impact of Generative AI on the Formal Writing Practices of Undergraduate Students,” tries to examine the extent, frequency, purposes, and perceived effects of Generative AI used by undergraduate students in formal writing. A descriptive survey research design along with a quantitative approach was applied. A structured online questionnaire was prepared using Google Forms to collect primary data from undergraduate students representing programmes such as B.A., BMS, BAF, B.Com., B.Sc. Computer Science, B.Sc. IT, Psychology, History, and B.A.M.M.C. A total of 108 responses were obtained. Non-probability convenience sampling was used, and responses were analysed on the basis of frequency and percentage analysis, along with interpretation of Likert-scale responses. The findings show that a considerable number of undergraduate students use Generative AI in formal writing practices, which is clear as 94 out of 108 respondents (86.9%) selecting previous use of Generative AI for formal writing. ChatGPT proved to be the most popular Generative AI tool used by the students, followed by Google Gemini and Claude. The study reveals students’ use of AI for generating ideas, drafting content, improving grammar and language, summarising information, and editing written work. This study is aimed at finding out the degree of AI help in formal writing, the level of students' improvement in their writing skills, confidence in writing without AI help, acceptance of AI-written content without major editing, and their readiness to keep using the tools. This study reveals the significance of Generative AI in the field of formal writing of undergraduates and the advantages, as well as possible drawbacks, connected to their dependence on the technology. These results can be helpful in studying the influence of Generative AI on the writing process of students and will help the educational institutions and teachers to encourage proper and ethical use of Generative AI by students.

documents.abstract: This study aimed to determine the influence of the learning environment on students’ achievement at Southern de Oro Philippines College, focusing specifically on peer influence, teacher approachability, and the availability of learning resources. The research adopted a correlational and causal design supplemented by documentary analysis. Data were gathered from 238 students across BSIT, CBAE, and CHTM programs during the 2025–2026 school year using a modified, validated questionnaire. Analysis involved descriptive statistics, correlation, and multiple linear regression to evaluate relationships and predictive effects. Findings revealed that the learning environment was generally rated high, with peer influence particularly strong, alongside favorable levels of teacher approachability and learning resources availability. Students’ achievement was also assessed at a satisfactory to good level. However, peer influence, teacher approachability, and learning resources availability showed no significant correlation or predictive influence on achievement. The study concludes that, despite a positive learning environment, these specific factors do not directly influence on students’ academic outcomes. Other variables, such as intrinsic motivation or external support systems, likely exert greater influence. Recommendations include peer mentoring initiatives and enhanced teacher training for better student engagement.

Abstract: Science has emerged as one of the most influential forces shaping economic growth, social transformation and national progress in the twenty-first century. The development of modern societies is increasingly dependent on the ability to create scientific knowledge, translate that knowledge into technological innovations and ensure that these innovations reach different sections of society. For a country such as India, which is simultaneously addressing issues of economic development, population growth, employment, education, healthcare, agriculture, energy security and environmental sustainability, science has a particularly important role to play. Scientific advancement can provide evidence-based and innovative solutions to complex national challenges while also strengthening India's competitiveness in the global knowledge economy. The vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 represents India's aspiration to become a developed nation by the centenary of independence. This vision encompasses not merely higher economic growth but also improvements in human development, education, healthcare, infrastructure, employment, social equity, technological capability, environmental sustainability and quality of life. Science and technology can serve as connecting forces among these different dimensions of development. Advances in agricultural science can improve productivity and climate resilience; medical science can support affordable healthcare; digital technologies can improve access to public services and education; space science can support communication, navigation and disaster management; renewable-energy research can strengthen energy security; and emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, biotechnology, robotics and quantum technologies can create new opportunities for innovation and economic growth. The present paper examines the multidimensional importance of science in India's development with particular reference to Viksit Bharat @2047. It adopts a descriptive and analytical approach based on secondary information obtained from policy documents, government reports, scientific institutions, educational literature and international development reports. The paper discusses the contribution of science to economic development, agriculture, healthcare, education, industry, digital transformation, space technology, renewable energy and environmental sustainability. It further explores the role of scientific education in developing curiosity, creativity, critical thinking, problem-solving ability and innovation among young people. The paper also identifies significant challenges, including unequal access to scientific resources, the digital divide, inadequate research infrastructure in some areas, limited industry-academia collaboration, shortage of specialised human resources, brain drain and the gap between scientific research and its practical application. The paper argues that the achievement of Viksit Bharat @2047 requires a transition from a technology-consuming society to a knowledge-generating and innovation-driven society. The article presents an improved methodological framework for the functional assessment of personal protective equipment (PPE) intended for humanitarian demining specialists. The relevance of the study is determined by the growing need for standardized and reproducible procedures for evaluating the ergonomic suitability, operational effectiveness, and functional compatibility of protective equipment used during mine action operations. Humanitarian demining activities are associated with increased physical, limited visibility, restricted mobility, and high operational risks; therefore, PPE must provide not only ballistic and fragmentation protection but also sufficient functionality for safe execution of demining tasks. The study analyzes the current Ukrainian regulatory and legal framework governing mine action activities and compares it with relevant international standards and technical recommendations. The conducted analysis demonstrates that existing Ukrainian legislation regulates organizational, managerial, and certification aspects of mine action but does not establish a dedicated methodology for evaluating the ergonomic and functional suitability of deminer PPE. This creates significant difficulties in conducting objective comparative testing and in making evidence-based decisions regarding operational applicability of protective equipment. The purpose of the research is to improve the methodological apparatus for functional evaluation of humanitarian demining PPE considering the requirements of Ukrainian legislation and international standards. The research methodology includes comparative regulatory analysis, classification of PPE systems, development of functional assessment procedures, and formalization of result interpretation algorithms. The proposed framework is based on the principles of functional representativeness, repeatability, traceability, and practical applicability of testing results. PPE systems are classified into light and heavy categories depending on their protective structure, mobility restrictions, and operational characteristics. The methodology introduces a structured matrix of functional tests, including emergency quick-release assessment, visor visibility evaluation, finger dexterity testing, manipulation with probing tools, mobility assessment, posture transition evaluation, and control of dangerous gaps between protective elements during movement. Particular attention is devoted to defining scoring criteria, minimum admissible thresholds, participant selection requirements, and averaging algorithms for individual and group assessment results. Mandatory and additional tests are differentiated according to PPE category and operational conditions. The methodology also establishes formalized rules for determining whether a PPE configuration satisfies functional suitability requirements. The practical applicability of the proposed approach is demonstrated through comparative assessment of two PPE configurations differing in torso protection design. The obtained results confirm that the methodology allows objective comparison of protective systems, improves reproducibility of testing procedures, and supports evidencebased selection of PPE for humanitarian demining operations. The developed methodological apparatus may be applied during certification procedures, procurement activities, comparative field trials, and further mathematical modeling of integrated PPE suitability indicators.

documents.abstract: End-to-end backpropagation has been the dominant mode of training in deep learning, allowing for the coordination of parameter updates across layers of a neural network. Prior studies have explored alternative -- and, in some cases, simpler -- training mechanisms, showing that they can sometimes achieve performance similar to backpropagation. However, the architectural conditions under which locally optimized networks, which avoid end-to-end backpropagation of error, can learn representations comparable to those learned through end-to-end training remain unclear. We aim to answer this question in the context of self-supervised learning, an important framework for large-scale pretraining in artificial intelligence. Here, we investigate how network width and depth affect the efficacy of greedy layer-wise and end-to-end self-supervised training in convolutional networks. We find that in wider networks, the benefits of end-to-end backpropagation over greedy layer-wise training shrink: in relatively shallow and very wide networks, we even observed higher performance in models trained with greedy layer-wise training. Subsequent analysis of the representations formed by these networks shows that very wide greedy-trained networks exhibit more favorable representational geometry than do networks trained end-to-end with backpropagation. This work shows that width can compensate for restricted credit assignment and identifies differences in representational geometry as a potential mechanism for their improved performance.

Population ageing has increased demand for long-term care, yet evidence on organizational and motivational correlates of work engagement among geriatric nursing assistants in China remains limited. Using convenience sampling, this cross-sectional survey recruited geriatric nursing assistants from nine aged care institutions in Xi’an and Weinan, Shaanxi Province, China, between May and August 2025. Of 396 returned questionnaires, 330 were included after prespecified data screening. Participants completed measures of perceived organizational climate, four work-motivation dimensions, and work engagement. Pearson correlations, observed-score regressions, four separate structural equation models, and 5,000-resample bias-corrected bootstrap analyses were conducted. Institution- and covariate-adjusted sensitivity analyses were also performed. In the joint regression model, intrinsic motivation ( β = 0.420, p < 0.001) and introjected regulation ( β = 0.324, p < 0.001) were independently associated with work engagement, whereas perceived organizational climate, identified regulation, and external regulation were not. Across the four structural equation models, perceived organizational climate was positively associated with each motivation dimension (standardized β = 0.652–0.704), and each motivation dimension was positively associated with work engagement ( β = 0.543–0.771). Because each model included only one motivation dimension, the indirect estimates were model-specific rather than unique contributions independent of the other dimensions. Significant indirect associations were observed through intrinsic motivation ( β = 0.519, bias-corrected 95% CI [0.430, 0.636]), identified regulation ( β = 0.430, [0.349, 0.532]), introjected regulation ( β = 0.530, [0.439, 0.648]), and external regulation ( β = 0.359, [0.258, 0.497]). In separate sensitivity analyses based on standardized observed scores, the four indirect associations remained statistically significant after adjustment for institutions and selected individual-level covariates. Perceived organizational climate and the four work-motivation dimensions were associated with work engagement among geriatric nursing assistants. The findings support further investigation of how organizational conditions and qualitatively different forms of work motivation relate to engagement. Because all variables were measured concurrently, temporal ordering and causal mediation cannot be established.

When inference demand exceeds available compute capacity, model providers must decide which requests should be served first. Users have different tolerances for delay from an LLM API, but current priority pricing schemes compress these differences into coarse fixed-price service tiers. We design an inference auction that allows users to bid for faster service. Our auction allocates priority in an economically efficient way without sacrificing latency, and we develop fast algorithms for implementing prices that incentivize truthful bidding. We also design an autobidding agent for our inference auction, where users specify an inference budget and the autobidder dynamically adjusts its bids over time to maximize user utility subject to the budget constraint. Experiments validate the practicality of our auction: it increases system welfare while maintaining the cache utilization and latency advantages of SGLang, a state-of-the-art inference serving framework.

The study analyzes the potential of generative AI technologies to address students' individual learning needs, differentiate instructional materials, develop English language skills (lexical, grammatical, communicative, and receptive-productive), provide immediate feedback, and support independent learning. The methodological framework of the study comprises systemic, comparative, linguo-didactic, and modeling methods. The results indicate that generative AI tools create additional opportunities for transitioning from a "one-size-fits-all" assignment approach to an individualized and differentiated teaching model in inclusive English language education. At the same time, issues such as the accuracy of AI-generated content, academic integrity, data privacy, the risk of excessive student reliance on AI, and the maintenance of teacher oversight were identified as critical methodological considerations.

ABSTRACT The development of foreign language communicative competence has become an essential component of contemporary higher education. The increasing internationalization of academic and professional environments requires university students to use foreign languages not only for understanding linguistic information but also for participating effectively in academic discussions, professional communication, intercultural interaction, collaborative projects, and digital communication. This article examines innovative approaches to developing students’ foreign language communicative competence in higher education. Particular attention is given to communicative, task-based, project-based, learner-centered, collaborative, and technology-enhanced approaches. The study analyzes the relationship between linguistic knowledge and practical communicative performance and identifies pedagogical conditions that contribute to students’ active participation in foreign language learning. The role of authentic materials, professional contexts, digital platforms, artificial intelligence, peer interaction, reflective learning, and formative assessment is also considered. The article proposes an integrated pedagogical framework in which foreign language instruction is organized around meaningful communicative tasks, learner autonomy, professional relevance, and continuous feedback. The proposed approach is intended to facilitate students’ transition from controlled language practice to independent and context-sensitive communication. Keywords: foreign language education, communicative competence, university students, innovative approaches, task-based learning, project-based learning, digital technologies, learner autonomy, intercultural communication, formative assessment.

documents.abstract: This review synthesises integrated strategies for safeguarding food and beverage safety, with emphasis on emerging contaminants, nutritional quality, and public health implications. Key contaminants, particularly microplastics (MPs) and synthetic dyes, are increasingly detected in packaged foods, bottled water, salt, and beverages, raising significant safety concerns. Recent studies reported a wide variability in MPs contamination across regions and food types, reflecting the absence of standardised detection protocols. Advances in analytical technologies, including nanomaterial-based electrochemical sensors, green microextraction techniques, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted detection platforms, have improved sensitivity and selectivity, although further validation and industrial scalability remain necessary. Similarly, research on synthetic dyes highlights progress in sustainable extraction and detection methods, such as deep eutectic solvent (DES) microextraction and sensor innovation, aligning with the growing shift toward eco-efficient analytical practices. This review also evaluates the nutritional and metabolic impacts of ultra-processed foods (UPFs), which represent a major component of modern diets and are consistently associated with obesity, metabolic syndrome, and other non-communicable diseases. Cross-country analyses revealed excessive sugar, salt, and fat content in UPFs, alongside gaps in front-of-package labelling systems and limited consumer literacy. These findings underscore the need for harmonised nutritional profiling frameworks and product reformulation policies. In addition, the role of probiotics in enhancing microbial safety and functional beverage quality is examined. Emerging microencapsulation techniques show promise in improving probiotic survival and bioactivity during storage and digestion, though mechanistic insights remain limited. Policy assessments indicate that fiscal measures, advertising regulations, and labelling requirements are inconsistently applied across nations, revealing persistent misalignment between technological innovations, regulatory implementation, and consumer behaviour. Three major research gaps are identified: (i) the lack of standardised, validated analytical methods for emerging contaminants; (ii) limited mechanistic understanding of probiotic stability and functionality in beverage systems; and (iii) insufficient integration of culturally adaptive, consumer-centred policy strategies. Future research should prioritise harmonised analytical frameworks, scalable and sustainable detection technologies, a clearer understanding of probiotic mechanisms, and comprehensive nutritional databases. Strong multisectoral collaboration among scientists, industry, and policymakers is crucial to translate these advances into effective public health actions. Collectively, this review highlights the need for an integrated, multidisciplinary approach that unites technological innovation, nutritional science, and evidence-based regulation to ensure the safety of food and beverages worldwide.

Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming education, research, industry and environmental decision-making, while climate change, biodiversity loss, pollution and resource stress demand ecological literacy and responsible innovation. This paper develops a multidisciplinary framework for integrating AI and Environmental Education in higher education under NEP 2020 to strengthen Education for Sustainable Development, green and digital skills, responsible innovation and Viksit Bharat @2047. The study uses a qualitative, conceptual and document-based design based on verified official and authoritative sources. India’s composite SDG Index score rose from 57 in 2018 to 71 in 2023–24; Maharashtra’s composite score in 2023–24 was 69. India had 1,028.61 million internet subscribers on 31 December 2025, while higher-education enrolment reached 4.50 crore in 2023–24. The proposed AI–EE–SDG–VB 2047 Framework is based on curriculum integration, capacity building, data and innovation, community engagement, and ethics and governance. The paper argues that technological progress must be accompanied by ecological intelligence, social inclusion and accountable human judgement.

The study uses a qualitative, conceptual and document-based design based on verified official and authoritative sources. India’s composite SDG Index score rose from 57 in 2018 to 71 in 2023–24; Maharashtra’s composite score in 2023–24 was 69. India had 1,028.61 million internet subscribers on 31 December 2025, while higher-education enrolment reached 4.50 crore in 2023–24. The proposed AI–EE–SDG–VB 2047 Framework is based on curriculum integration, capacity building, data and innovation, community engagement, and ethics and governance. The paper argues that technological progress must be accompanied by ecological intelligence, social inclusion and accountable human judgement.

Abstract The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), first-principles computational methods, and advanced functional materials provides new opportunities for the accelerated discovery of energy-efficient quantum and spintronic materials. Heusler alloys are particularly attractive because their chemical composition and structural ordering can be systematically modified to obtain desirable magnetic, electronic, topological, and thermoelectric properties. Magnetic Heusler compounds with strong spin–orbit coupling can exhibit Weyl points, band crossings, Berry-curvature hotspots, and enhanced anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) and anomalous Nernst conductivity (ANC). Representative literature systems demonstrate the potential of this materials family: Co2MnGa has a reported calculated AHC of approximately −1310 Scm⁻¹, while Co2MnAl reaches approximately −1631 Scm⁻¹; Co2CrAl illustrates strong Fermi-level dependence, with its AHC increasing from approximately −313 Scm⁻¹ to about 1089 Scm⁻¹ after energy tuning. This work proposes an integrated density functional theory (DFT) and AI framework for the systematic discovery and optimization of sustainable topological Heusler materials. DFT calculations provide the physics-based evaluation of structural stability, magnetic ordering, electronic structure, spin–orbit coupling, Berry curvature, AHC, and ANC, while machine-learning models can learn composition–structure–property relationships and accelerate screening across unexplored chemical spaces. The proposed workflow includes stability screening, magnetic-ground-state analysis, electronic and topological characterization, Berry-curvature calculations, anomalous transverse transport calculations, machine-learning prediction, and independent DFT validation. Chemical substitution and carrier tuning are considered as strategies for positioning topological features near the Fermi level and enhancing transverse transport. Literature examples such as Pt2CrRh, with reported AHC of approximately 1966 Scm⁻¹ and ANC of approximately 7.50 Am⁻¹K⁻¹, and (Co0. 8Ni0.2)2FeSn, with reported AHC of approximately −2568 Scm⁻¹ and ANC of approximately 8.27 Am⁻¹K⁻¹, illustrate the potential of chemical tuning for achieving large transverse responses. The proposed DFT–AI strategy can therefore provide an efficient route toward identifying promising materials for spintronics, spin-caloritronics, low-power electronics, and thermal-energy conversion.

documents.abstract: Digital transformation has become a strategic priority for higher education institutions (HEIs), with blended learning environments (BLEs) increasingly positioned as sustainable approaches that combine online and face-to-face learning. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly entering these environments, offering opportunities for personalised guidance, adaptive learning support, automated feedback, and enhanced media design. However, AI adoption often remains fragmented and technology-driven, creating challenges related to pedagogical coherence, ethics, equity, and sustainability. This paper argues that AI integration in blended courses should be understood as a maturity process rather than as a question of technology adoption alone. Using the European Maturity Model for Blended Education Plus (EMBED+) as an analytical framework, this study explores how AI-supported practices can evolve across maturity stages. The analysis focuses on two course-level dimensions where AI has particular relevance: Blended Learner Guidance and Use of Media and Tools. Through a conceptual mapping approach, AI applications are aligned with four maturity stages: ad hoc, deliberate, responsive, and embedded. Findings indicate that mature AI integration is characterised not by advanced technologies, but by intentional pedagogical design, evidence-informed improvement, and adaptive deployment. The proposed framework provides educators, instructional designers, and institutional leaders with a shared language to evaluate and strengthen AI-enhanced blended learning practices.

The article critically analyzes and scientifically substantiates the paradigm of integrating modern information and communication technologies (ICT) and artificial intelligence (AI) tools into the system of heuristic foreign language teaching in higher education. The author demonstrates that the synergy of digital tools and generative AI serves as a powerful intensifier of the educational process, ensuring deep individualization, differentiation of learning, enhancement of students’ intrinsic motivation, and the development of their cognitive and creative autonomy. The study synthesizes practical experience in utilizing the digital ecosystem of Sumy State Pedagogical University named after A.S. Makarenko in combination with video conferencing services (Google Meet, Zoom) and adaptive AI technologies to organize flexible online learning. Particular attention is paid to the effectiveness of these tools under crisis conditions (the COVID-19 pandemic and martial law) both for the routine automation of assessment and for modeling open-ended creative tasks of an exploratory nature. The paper presents original methodological developments, including the electronic manual «Communicative Culture of Medical Students in Use», integrated with modern digital resources. Specific examples demonstrate how the use of ICT and AI assistants enables students to complete a full heuristic cycle: from analytical information processing to the generation, self-correction, and defense of their own original educational product. The author summarizes the undeniable advantages of the updated innovative higher education space, which transforms traditional subject-subject relations into a format of interactive partnership: “teacher – student – artificial intelligence”.
topics: Innovations in Education and Learning Technologies

documents.abstract: Abstract This chapter discusses how Large Language Models (LLMs) like ChatGPT can be used in modern foreign language teaching. It focusses on teacher training in integrative approaches that do not see LLMs as supplementary learning, but as part of the central teacher–learner interaction, including autonomous learning in flipped classroom approaches. It is not an empirical study with students, but an empirical play with prompts, the decisive starting point of successful human–machine/artificial intelligence/chatbot interaction. It emphasizes the potential of LLMs for teaching and learning without neglecting ethical concerns and practical challenges. It provides examples from ChatGPT 3–5 and Bard Experiment, now Gemini, to illustrate how LLMs can be used to generate explanations, construct exercises with model answers and even correct exam tests for complex grammatical English constructions such as article usage and modal auxiliaries. This study illustrates where LLMs can be integrated into teacher training to help students in autonomous or teacher-mediated learning, but it also shows clearly that users always have to be well-informed and remain skeptical about LLM suggestions and that even LLMs in their current free versions only provide suggestions that may only be used in revised or adapted form.

documents.abstract: The maritime industry is undergoing a paradigm shift driven by stringent decarbonization regulations, such as the Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) and Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI). Despite the proliferation of technical solutions, a conceptual divide persists between emission compliance and the established safety management culture governed by the International Safety Management (ISM) Code. This study employs a comprehensive bibliometric analysis to examine the intellectual structure and evolution of the maritime decarbonization literature. Using a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-guided selection process, 88 core publications from the Web of Science database were analyzed using R Bibliometrix. Results from the Gompertz growth model suggest a trend toward technical saturation in the literature, pointing to a potential shift toward operational management. Furthermore, factorial and Sankey analyses reveal a significant disconnect between emissions management and Safety Management Systems (SMS), with “human factors” and “safety culture” remaining marginalized as “niche” themes. The findings suggest that decarbonization is currently treated as an external “administrative reporting burden” rather than an organic operational routine. To bridge this gap, this study conceptualizes the pathways for integrating operational emission management into SMS from an ISM Code perspective. Rather than proposing isolated technical data fixes or validated operational software, the study illustrates how fuel inefficiencies can be conceptually evaluated within the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) cycle. This research provides a baseline for policymakers and ship management companies seeking to align environmental performance monitoring with shipboard safety routines.

Background The high variability of workloads makes it very difficult for cloud datacenters to efficiently schedule their tasks and resource allocation. The correct forecasting of future resource utilization allows us to proactively scale and implement more sophisticated scheduling policies, which eventually results in has potential to improve resource utilization and fewer failures. Methods Leveraging only data that is exposed to the scheduler at task dispatch times, this research assesses four supervised learning approaches for estimation of CPU consumption on the Google Cluster Data v3 trace: Linear Regression, Support Vector Regression, Random Forest, and a Neural Network. Result The randomized forest version gave the optimum regression performances on a held-out test set (MAE ≈ 0.00233, RMSE ≈ 0.00589, R 2 ≈ 0.895), while an ordinary hybrid composition of the two best systems performed similarly. Estimating if a task’s real CPU consumption surpasses a train-set-derived high utilization threshold which was achieved up to 0.921 accuracy and ≈ 0.844 best F1, chosen via a detailed threshold sweeping as opposed to an individual set cutoff. Conclusions This approach are evaluated using RMSE, MAE, and R 2 for held-out on test set, while the 2nd threshold-based analysis is utilized to appraise the recognition of high-CPU tasks. These results underscore the potential of data driven approach definitely machine and deep learning-based CPU demand predictions as valuable tools for cloud schedulers, improving resource management, and reducing operational costs. Also discuss the feasibility of deploying the proposed solution on distributed platforms such as Spark and Google Cloud and outline future research directions to integrate predictive models with real-time cloud resource management.

This study aimed to evaluate health science students’ intentions to adopt artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare and to identify key predictors of these intentions using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 967 students enrolled in various health-related disciplines at a university. Data were collected through a self-administered online questionnaire comprising five sections: demographic information, information technology (IT) skills, perceptions of AI in medicine, attitudes towards AI and intentions to adopt AI in healthcare. Approximately half of the participants reported high intentions to integrate AI into their future medical practice. Linear regression analyses confirmed the applicability of the TAM in predicting AI adoption intentions and identified the following three significant predictors: attitudes towards AI, perceptions of AI in medicine and IT skills. Among these, attitudes towards AI emerged as the strongest predictor (β = 0.563, t = 17.687, p < 0.001). These findings underscore the importance of fostering students’ IT competencies and positive perceptions and attitudes to facilitate the effective integration of AI into medical education and practice. Future research should employ longitudinal designs to examine changes in students’ perceptions and attitudes over time, thereby providing insights for curriculum development that better aligns with students’ evolving learning needs and ensures professional readiness.

Motivation is crucial in enhancing pupils’ interest, engagement, and positive experiences in science education. This study employed a descriptive quantitative research design to examine the intrinsic and extrinsic motivation of Grade 3 pupils in selected elementary schools in the Santa Fe District, Nueva Vizcaya. Intrinsic motivation was evaluated based on interest in science, curiosity, desire to learn, enjoyment of science activities, and self-confidence. Extrinsic motivation factors included teacher support and encouragement, rewards and recognition, classroom environment, and availability of learning materials. The research also identified obstacles impacting pupils’ motivation to learn science. Data were collected using a researcher-developed questionnaire and analyzed using frequency, percentage, mean, and standard deviation (SD). The findings provide a foundation for identifying motivational strengths and areas needing further support in science education. These results underscore the importance of creating engaging classroom experiences, providing appropriate learning resources, strengthening teacher support, and maintaining a positive learning environment that encourages active participation in science activities. Based on the identified motivational needs and obstacles, a motivation-based intervention program was proposed to enhance pupils’ intrinsic and extrinsic motivation and support meaningful science learning. The findings may offer teachers and school administrators practical guidance in developing learning experiences that foster pupils’ interest, curiosity, enjoyment, confidence, and sustained engagement in science.

The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming learning design, yet current terminology often lacks the precision to distinguish between varying levels of AI involvement. Terms like "AI-supported" obscure critical differences in decision-making authority and adaptation dynamism. This presentation introduces the LISA Framework (Level of autonomy and Interaction Scope of AI in learning design), developed within the Erasmus+ project DigiSET. LISA proposes a two-dimensional typology based on (1) the Level of AI Autonomy (human-led assistance to fully autonomous operation) and (2) the Interaction Scope (static, rule-based execution vs. dynamic, comprehensive adaptation). Six archetypes emerge: the Content Generator, the Co-Creator, the Rule-Based Agent, the Smart Assistant, the Adaptive Partner, and the Autonomous Agent. Grounded in practical experiences from Graz University of Technology, this heuristic model provides educators, researchers, and policymakers with a structured vocabulary to analyze, discuss, and strategically plan AI-enhanced learning resources. documents.abstract: Problem. Ensuring the technosphere safety of industrial facilities in the oil and gas sector is complicated by processes of hidden microstructural degradation of metal, which initiates more than 31 % of emergency situations. Traditional nondestructive testing methods are significantly limited by the need for thorough surface preparation and ensuring stable liquid acoustic contact, which hinders the operational monitoring of pipelines and pressure ves sels through insulation layers. Aim. The aim of this study is to establish quantitative relationships between the spectral parameters of the electromagnetic-acoustic (EMA) signal and the stages of stress-strain state and damage of structural steels. Methods. A series of experiments was performed on St3sp, 09G2S, and 12Kh18N10T steels under static tension on a servohydraulic system. Signal registration was carried out using an EMA thickness gauge. The analysis is based on dynamic approach: the control zone was identified as a linear system, the mathematical reference of which is a secondorder transfer function W(p) reconstructed by the method of moments. To automate state recognition, a transition to frequency models in the form of hodographs of amplitude-phase-frequency characteristics (APFC) was implemented. An artificial neural network based on the ML.NET library was trained on 3 samples of 720 measurements, using the amplitudes and phases of the first 15 signal harmonics as input features. Results. It was experimentally proved that the accumulation of structural damage causes a regular migration of the roots of the characteristic polynomial on the complex plane and a qualitative transformation of the shape of the APFC hodographs. The developed intelligent classifier provided an identification accuracy of the stress-strain state (SSS) stages at the level of 92.16 %, while the error in determining the numerical stress values did not exceed 3.5 %. Conclusions. The spectral parameters of the EMA signal in combination with machine learning technologies make it possible to identify reliably pre-defect states of metal. The proposed method minimises the influence of the human factor and ensures the detection of zones of critical stress concentration before the initiation of macroscopic cracks.

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as automated judges for AI-generated content, yet a single judge is unreliable and even a panel of judges leaves a hard residue: when judges disagree, majority voting discards the conflict instead of resolving it. We present JuryFlow, a disagreement-guided, human-in-the-loop multi-agent evaluation framework that treats inter-judge disagreement not as noise to be averaged away, but as a precise, claim-level signal indicating where an evaluation is uncertain. JuryFlow decomposes each candidate response into atomic claims, has a panel of heterogeneous judges assign per-claim verdicts, and builds a disagreement graph whose nodes are scored by verdict entropy and whose edges encode structural similarity between claims. A human acts as a structural guide, selecting which disagreement to resolve through a single, minimal intervention rather than re-labeling the response, after which the focal claim is re-evaluated, the correction propagates along graph edges and to historically similar cases, and is crystallized into reusable rubric entries that all judges inherit, making the evaluator progressively self-refining. To enable large-scale, reproducible benchmarking without human studies, we evaluate JuryFlow in an automatic configuration in which focal selection is made by entropy ranking. On MT-Bench and LLMBar, JuryFlow improves agreement with gold labels over single-judge and majority-vote panel baselines, and ablations isolate the contributions of disagreement-targeted re-evaluation, propagation, and rubric induction. We contribute (1) a human-in-the-loop paradigm that recasts the human from labeler to structural guide, (2) the JuryFlow framework operationalizing it through a disagreement graph, focal re-evaluation, and closed-loop rubric induction, and (3) an evaluation protocol with ablations that isolate where the gains originate.

documents.abstract: This article analyzes the determinative role of occupational health in individual psychological well-being from a socio-psychological perspective. Professional activity, as an essential component of human life, significantly influences emotional state, stress resilience, and overall psychological stability. The study explores the relationship between occupational health indicators and psychological well-being using empirical methods. The results show that a healthy work environment enhances psychological stability and life satisfaction.

Purpose This study aims to examine how healthcare professionals responsible for training (HPRTs) interpret and appropriate artificial intelligence (AI)-focused pedagogical resources within their workplace context, addressing the knowing-doing gap: the pattern whereby increased awareness of AI tools does not straightforwardly translate into changed practice and may recalibrate professional confidence even as perceived relevance increases. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative intervention design was used at the Centre hospitalier de l’Université de Montréal (CHUM). Six participants of differing prior AI experience engaged with an eight-week intervention delivering pedagogical guides and microlearning videos. Data were collected through two focus group discussions conducted in French and analysed on original transcripts using reflexive thematic analysis, with Illeris’s workplace learning theory as primary sensitising framework, alongside situated expectancy-value, personal construct and agency theories, drawn on iteratively. Findings Three findings emerged, differentiated by participant experience level: (1) expectancy recalibration, in which increased knowledge accompanied decreased confidence, marking accommodative learning; (2) principled boundary-setting, through which professionals differentiated between appropriate and inappropriate AI uses; and (3) organisational conditions, namely, tool access, protected time and institutional endorsement, as important structural mediators of literacy development. Originality/value The study conceptualises the knowing-doing gap as an emergent structural feature of AI literacy development under real organisational conditions, extending the literature by documenting learners’ experience of that gap. Reduced confidence may signal more differentiated professional judgment rather than failure. Individual learning capacity requires an infrastructure of agency for realisation. These findings challenge adoption-centric models of professional AI literacy.

documents.abstract: The entry of large language models (LLMs) into social science research practices, such as interview coding, literature reviews, hypothesis generation and the simulation of respondents, is usually discussed from a technical or ethical standpoint. This paper offers an epistemological reading. It argues that an LLM is neither a neutral instrument nor a "co-researcher", but an interpretive mediator whose probabilistic and opaque outputs affect the criteria of rigour differently depending on the paradigm adopted. By confronting LLM uses with the positivist, critical realist, interpretivist and constructivist paradigms, the paper shows that each paradigm calls for specific safeguards. It then proposes a protocol for comparing human and algorithmic coding, followed by a five-dimension rigour framework (traceability, reproducibility, reflexivity, adversarial validation and interpretive accountability) specified for each paradigm. The contribution is twofold. Theoretically, the paper brings generative AI into the debate on the foundations of knowledge in the social sciences. Methodologically, it provides researchers and reviewers with a tool to assess the legitimacy of AI-assisted research.

documents.abstract: Generative recommendation, has been attracted a surge of attentions in industrial and academic research community, towards to build more smart system to build next-generation recommender. Under the significant developing wave of large language model, our team have been developed Semantic ID based OneRec/OneRec-V2. These models have been widely deployed in production and demonstrate the scaling potential of the autoregressive next-item prediction paradigm for industrial recommender systems. Building on the success of OneRec, we further explored a series of models, including OneRec-Think, OpenOneRec, and OneReason, that connect item Semantic IDs with natural language in a unified representation space and seek to unlock the potential of natural-language chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning for recommendation. However, our preliminary works found that introducing reasoning CoT does not always improve the recommendation performance. To address this issue, OneReason strengthens the semantic alignment between items and language, introduces structured template-based supervision for interest reasoning, and applies advanced reinforcement learning techniques to make reasoning more beneficial to recommendation. As a frontier topic to building recommendation foundation models, we believe this topic has significant research value and hope to encourage more researchers to explore it together. To this end, together with the SIGIR 2026 community, we organized the KUAISHOU Explorer LLM-Rec Challenge 2026: Reasoning Generative Recommendation.

La incorporación de la inteligencia artificial en el bachillerato transforma la búsqueda de información, la realización de tareas y la comprensión de contenidos, aunque también plantea riesgos de dependencia, uso acrítico y afectación de la integridad académica. El estudio tiene como objetivo analizar la influencia percibida de la inteligencia artificial sobre el rendimiento académico de los estudiantes de tercero de bachillerato de la Unidad Educativa Cristiana Nazareno. Se emplea un enfoque mixto secuencial, iniciado con una revisión documental cualitativa y continuado con una fase cuantitativa mediante una encuesta estructurada con escala Likert; el diseño es no experimental, transversal y de alcance exploratorio-descriptivo, con una muestra censal de 32 estudiantes. La simulación de resultados muestra que 21 participantes utilizan inteligencia artificial frecuentemente o siempre, 17 prefieren ChatGPT, 22 la emplean para investigar y 21 perciben mejoras en la comprensión y el aprendizaje; asimismo, 22 reconocen riesgo de dependencia. Estos hallazgos evidencian una valoración favorable, aunque no permiten establecer causalidad entre uso de inteligencia artificial y calificaciones. Se concluye que estas herramientas constituyen un apoyo académico relevante, siempre que se integren con orientación docente, verificación de información y criterios de uso responsable.

Abstract Toxicity prediction in small molecules represents a fundamental challenge in drug development and chemical safety assessment. Traditional approaches heavily rely on predefined molecular descriptors or fingerprints, potentially limiting the ability to capture complex and nonlinear structure–activity relationships. Here, we present a descriptor-free, language-inspired framework that can be applied to different toxicity prediction tasks within a unified architecture. The model proposed combines a multiscale Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) layer to capture chemical patterns at different scales and a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) layer to capture the sequential nature of these patterns. This architecture also exploits an attention mechanism that computes attention weights across the sequence, enabling the model to focus on the most relevant molecular substructures for toxicity prediction. Toxic and nontoxic chemicals, represented by canonical SMILES, are investigated as the words of two languages which have to be discriminated; using eight different end points, the model provided an accurate description of toxicity patterns, with an average Area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.83 (min: 0.70, max: 0.94) under repeated cross-validation. The models were trained on relatively small data sets (∼1000 samples) and often strongly imbalanced, two important challenges that highlight the opportunities for future improvement; moreover, the proposed attention-based framework offers a representation of the molecular regions influencing model predictions, providing a basis for future investigations into toxicity-related structural patterns and potentially supporting hypothesis generation in drug design or drug repurposing applications.

The rapid expansion of scientific publications and patent filings challenges conventional approaches for systematically assessing technological progress in emerging energy storage technologies. Here, we present an artificial intelligence-assisted patent analytics framework to identify technology-specific research gaps (“white spots”), using zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs) and organic electrode materials (OEMs) as representative case studies. Patents were classified across multiple analytical dimensions, including materials, battery chemistries, and key performance indicators (KPIs). Three analytically distinct types of white spots are identified: limited absolute patenting activity within a given category (activity white spots), insufficient quantitative performance disclosure despite active patenting (reporting white spots), and disproportionate reliance on knowledge transferred from adjacent battery fields (knowledge-flow white spots). The analysis reveals a strong dominance of aqueous electrolyte concepts in ZIBs, accounting for 1883 patents, while non-aqueous and solid electrolytes remain underrepresented. Citation network analysis further shows that innovation in these underexplored electrolyte classes relies disproportionately on knowledge originating from adjacent battery technologies. For OEMs, up to 93% of the 368 patents focus on lithium-based chemistries, which exhibit the most comprehensive quantitative reporting. In contrast, sodium-based and all-solid-state systems are characterized by substantial gaps in KPI disclosure, limiting cross-chemistry benchmarking. Overall, the results demonstrate that white spots in emerging battery technologies arise not only at the materials level, but also from asymmetric knowledge flows and incomplete performance reporting. The here proposed framework provides a scalable tool for mapping technological maturity and supporting research strategies in next-generation energy storage systems.

Aim/objective This study aimed to classify subgroups of artificial intelligence (AI) anxiety among nursing undergraduates using latent profile analysis, describe their demographic characteristics, and identify factors associated membership in each latent profile. Background Artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely implemented in clinical nursing practice, but nursing undergraduates often experience AI anxiety, which impedes their adaptation to smart medical services. Few existing studies have stratified students according to anxiety levels to formulate targeted intervention measures. Design A cross-sectional study. Methods Participants were 526 nursing undergraduates recruited from several medical colleges in Jiangxi, Hunan, Hubei, and Sichuan provinces as well as Chongqing Municipality, China. Questionnaires, including a general information questionnaire, the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale, and the Artificial Intelligence Self-Efficacy Questionnaire, were distributed. Mplus version 8.3 was used for latent profile analysis, and multinomial logistic regression was performed to analyze factors associated with profile membership. Results A total of 526 students were included. The total AI anxiety score was 57.76 ± 15.94, indicating a moderate level of AI anxiety. AI anxiety among undergraduate nursing students was classified into three latent profiles: the low AI anxiety group (53.2%), moderate AI anxiety group (12.7%), and high AI anxiety group (34.0%). Multinomial logistic regression analysis showed that gender, participation in AI-related education or courses, attitude toward AI, and monthly household income (Renminbi [RMB]) were independently associated with membership in latent profiles among undergraduate nursing students with AI anxiety ( p < 0.05). Conclusion Nursing undergraduates present distinct heterogeneous patterns of AI anxiety. These findings may help identify students with elevated AI anxiety and inform individualized educational interventions.

documents.abstract: ABSTRACT Lawsone is a naturally occurring naphthoquinone mainly obtained from the leaves of Lawsonia inermis (henna). It is responsible for the characteristic orange-red colour of henna and has attracted interest because of its chemical reactivity, natural origin, analytical importance and biological properties. Chemically, lawsone is known as 2-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone and contains a conjugated quinone system with hydroxyl and carbonyl functional groups. Large language models are increasingly used as collaborators on deductive-reasoning tasks, but their outputs can hallucinate or pull users away from intended reasoning. Formal proof assistants provide machine-checked verification, but have a steep learning curve and require more granular reasoning than human written proofs. We explore an interface that combines these strengths, allowing users to write and revise free-form natural-language proofs while a verified backend checks their reasoning and returns feedback at the user's granularity. We study this interface in the context of undergraduate mathematics education by developing LeanSide, a formally verified co-reasoning system, which auto-formalizes student reasoning into Lean and informalizes verifier output into understandable feedback. We conducted user studies through classroom deployment and analyzed which system properties helped students make progress and which caused them to get stuck. We use these findings to derive design implications for using a formally verified backend in human-AI co-reasoning systems.

documents.abstract: Abstract The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping language learning environments, yet little is known about how it becomes embedded within learners' motivational and agentive experiences in collaborative, informal settings like English drama‐based learning. This qualitative case study examines EFL learners' motivation during a 12‐week GenAI‐mediated English drama production cycle in a Chinese university drama club. Guided by Dörnyei's (2009) L2 Motivational Self System (L2MSS), the analysis examines learners' accounts of the Ideal L2 Self, Ought‐to L2 Self, and L2 Learning Experience alongside three analytic patterns of agency identified in this case: authorship, judgment, and collaboration. Data were drawn from focus groups, individual interviews, drama scripts, GenAI interaction artifacts, and rehearsal observations. Findings indicate that participants experienced GenAI as part of their motivational ecology, particularly in relation to access to advanced language, emerging reference points for “good English,” and the ways collaborative decisions were negotiated. Participants also described different ways of maintaining ownership, evaluating GenAI‐generated language, and coordinating decisions with others. The study extends L2 motivational research by revealing how L2MSS dimensions acquire context‐specific meanings in GenAI‐mediated drama‐based language learning and underscores the importance of fostering critical judgment and sustained human collaboration in GenAI‐supported language learning.

Student Engagement refers to the degree to which learners actively participate in educational activities, interact with learning resources, communicate with teachers and peers, and remain involved in the learning process. In digital education, Learning Analytics can provide systematic methods for observing and analysing different forms of student engagement. Traditional measures of engagement often depend on classroom observation, attendance, participation, assignments, and teacher feedback. Digital learning environments can provide additional information through learning management systems, online assessments, discussion platforms, virtual laboratories, educational applications, and connected learning devices. Learning Analytics can transform these data into meaningful information that helps teachers understand patterns of participation and identify opportunities to support student learning. A simplified framework is: Student Activity → Data Collection → Learning Analytics → Engagement Pattern → Teacher Interpretation → Educational SupportThe purpose of engagement analytics should not be simply to count student activities. The central goal is to understand whether students are meaningfully participating in learning and whether additional support may be required. Student engagement represents the learner's active involvement in the educational process. It can include: Participation Attention Interaction Motivation Collaboration Persistence Completion of learning activities Engagement is multidimensional and cannot be completely represented by a single numerical indicator. Student engagement is commonly considered through several dimensions: Behavioural engagement Cognitive engagement Emotional engagement Social engagement These dimensions can interact with one another. Behavioural engagement refers to observable participation in learning activities. Examples include: Attending classes Completing assignments Participating in activities Submitting assessments Accessing learning resources Digital systems can record some of these activities. Cognitive engagement refers to the mental effort students invest in understanding and applying knowledge.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools are reshaping how students approach problem-solving in programming education. This study demonstrated the methodological value of metaphor analysis in examining students’ perceptions of AI-supported learning. It explored how first-year students in an introductory Python programming module at a South African university conceptualize GenAI use during coding-related tasks. The context matters because many students from disadvantaged communities enter university with limited computing exposure. Guided by a framework of AI-mediated cognitive engagement, the study drew on 161 responses and used inductive-deductive metaphor analysis to examine how students position AI in relation to their thinking. Six dominant metaphorical framings emerged: tool, tutor, facilitator, specialist, liar, and threat. These metaphors revealed that students experienced AI in both constructive and cautionary ways, as a source of cognitive support and conceptual expansion, and as a potential source of reduced mental effort. The findings showed a systematic correspondence between metaphorical framings and reported cognitive experiences, including mind-mending, mind-stretching, mind-gaming, and mind-replacement. Chi-square and Fisher’s exact tests strengthened the qualitative findings by confirming an association between metaphor roles and cognitive influence. The study contributes to research on AI in education by showing that metaphor offers a powerful lens for understanding how students interpret and regulate AI-supported learning. It argues that GenAI is a conditional cognitive mediator whose impact depends on student agency, epistemic trust, and the nature of engagement. The findings have implications for the design of programming curricula and educational practices, integrating AI responsibly while sustaining critical thinking and academic integrity.

Modern transformers pair impressive capabilities with substantial memory and compute demands. Low-rank weight factorization reduces both while keeping the matrices dense, and thus efficient on standard hardware. Existing methods, however, choose the subspace to remove from each weight matrix with local closed-form criteria: activation energy, layer-wise reconstruction error, or a quadratic approximation of the loss. These criteria ignore how errors propagate through the network, so at high compression the errors compound with depth and performance collapses. We introduce Learnable Subspace Projections (LSP), which instead learns the subspaces to discard end-to-end. Each linear layer, or tied group of layers that read the same activations, is assigned an orthogonal projector. All projectors are optimized jointly against a global objective--the KL divergence to the dense model's output distribution or the model's original training loss--while the pretrained weights remain frozen. Projectors are initialized from a whitened SVD truncation, and ranks are allocated by the output KL each projector induces per parameter saved. After training, the projectors merge into standard low-rank factors, with each tied group sharing one factor. In attention, this also lets the model cache one narrow latent in place of full keys and values. Across LLMs (OPT-125M/1.3B, Qwen3-4B, Llama-2-7B) and ViT-B/16, LSP outperforms baselines, and its advantage widens as compression increases. At -70% compression, LSP brings Llama-2-7B to 10.9 WikiText-2 perplexity and 42.2% mean zero-shot accuracy, versus 13.3 and 36.0% for the strongest baseline. The factorized model decodes up to 1.6x faster than the dense model at small batch sizes, and aching the shared latent shrinks the combined memory of weights and KV cache by 13.5x at a 128k-token context, versus at most 6.5x for untied baseline factorizations.

Chain-of-thought monitoring as an approach for AI oversight and control is threatened by the possibility of steganographic reasoning, where LLMs conceal their reasoning inside innocuous-looking text. Two neighbouring capabilities, steganographic messaging (passing a concealed message) and encoded reasoning (reasoning in an illegible but unconcealed format), have already been shown to emerge under training pressures that occur in real pipelines, such as reinforcement learning against monitors. This suggests that steganographic reasoning too might arise as an unintended side effect of training. Here, we compare how easily models learn steganographic reasoning and these two neighbouring capabilities across three elicitation methods: reinforcement learning, in-context learning, and supervised fine-tuning (SFT). For most tasks, models learn steganographic reasoning only under SFT, while they learn steganographic messaging and encoded reasoning under all three elicitation methods. Even under SFT, steganographic reasoning requires at least twice as much training as messaging, and for several model-task combinations it is not learned at all. However, on a cover task that makes hiding information especially convenient, steganographic reasoning can be successfully learned under all three elicitation methods. Steganographic reasoning is thus much harder than steganographic messaging and encoded reasoning, and learning the latter two does not imply learning the former. Yet it lies within reach: an easy version is learned under every elicitation method, when the cover task is convenient for hiding information.

documents.abstract: Omni-modal large language models (OmniLLMs) enable unified audio-video understanding, but their long multimodal token sequences make deployment computationally expensive. Token compression reduces this cost, yet aggressive compression often lowers accuracy. Existing works predominantly focus on designing better compression mechanisms; however, adapting the underlying language model to reason effectively over the remaining compressed context remains under-explored. To address this, we propose CAFD (Compressed-Context Adaptation via Full-Context Distillation), a ground-truth-free self-distillation framework that adapts OmniLLMs to fixed compression pipelines without requiring reference answers, rationales, or correctness rewards. CAFD leverages the full-token view of the same multimodal sample as a source of privileged information: a full-context self-teacher provides soft target supervision to a compressed-context student along the student's on-policy trajectory. Evaluated on Qwen2.5-Omni-7B across five audio-video benchmarks, five compression pipelines, and five deployment budgets, CAFD demonstrates consistent gains, improving 120 out of 125 conditions with an average accuracy boost of 1.44 points and recovering 26.9% of the accuracy gap on average. These results demonstrate that the proposed ground-truth-free adaptation offers an effective and practical route to improving the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in deployed OmniLLMs.

LLM agents rely on retrieval tools to access external knowledge, yet visual agentic search remains severely bottlenecked by standard single-step retrievers. In current pipelines, the agent must issue text queries for every intermediate step, struggling when visual clues are difficult to describe or when the retriever fails to surface necessary intermediate evidence within its top results. We hypothesize that offloading multi-step navigation across the entire embedding space directly to the retrieval tool resolves this performance bottleneck. To study this systematically, we introduce VHOP, a flexible data generation framework and benchmark with five core difficulty levels testing both visual matching and search planning. Using this framework, we develop VHOP-Router, an end-to-end training pipeline---combining supervised fine-tuning, online imitation learning, and reinforcement learning---that transforms a standard embedding model into an autoregressive multi-step retriever. Operating directly in the visual latent space, VHOP-Router retrieves linked image chains in a single tool call without requiring the agent to formulate intermediate text queries. Experiments show VHOP-Router boosts retrieval performance from under 5\% to 76.3\%. In agentic search, it improves task success rates by 52.7\% and reduces the average token length by 61\% from 1886 to 728, whereas upgrading the agent yields only a 3.7\% gain. Compared to a strong baseline where the agent retrieves the top 50 results per step, VHOP-Router maintains superior performance while reducing in-context images by $23\times$ and cutting the cumulative API payload by $35\times$. The models also generalize robustly to unseen difficulty levels and realistic test sets. Ultimately, VHOP and VHOP-Router provide an efficient and effective solution for visual agentic search that leaves native LLM capabilities entirely intact.
topics: Advanced Image and Video Retrieval Techniques

documents.abstract: Machine learning systems increasingly face the need to remove the influence of entire data domains, such as toxic language, harmful behavior, or topical content, rather than isolated records. Recent work formalizes this problem as \emph{distributional unlearning}: selecting a subset of a forget domain whose removal moves the training distribution away from an unwanted population while preserving proximity to the desired one. However, existing analyses often impose parametric assumptions to obtain tractable selection rules. These assumptions may be poorly suited to high-dimensional language-model representations. We introduce \textsc{Mamushi}, a framework for non-parametric distributional unlearning that ranks forget examples using a probabilistic classifier whose Bayes-optimal logit equals the forget-to-retain log-density ratio (up to an additive class-prior constant). We show that thresholding the population log-density ratio yields the optimal fixed-budget selection rule for our removal--preservation objective and establish a non-asymptotic transfer guarantee relating score-estimation and threshold-calibration errors to degradation from the population-optimal selection rule. Our empirical evaluation spans real-world datasets on toxic-language removal and topical-domain removal regimes using different representations, with \textsc{Mamushi} achieving a more favorable removal--preservation trade-off than other baselines. Our work shows that \textsc{Mamushi} can serve as an efficient selection approach for downstream machine unlearning procedures, reducing the number of forget examples required to reach a fixed forgetting target.
